ex.en: It's better to book in advance.
If you're running late, let me know ahead of time.
Thanks for telling me ahead of time.
What do you do for a living?
I'm a nurse by profession.
My dad travels a lot for work.

fix.note: 으-irregular: 기뻐요. For someone else's joy, use 기뻐하다.

ex.en: I'm so happy to see you again.
I was so happy to hear I'd passed.
I'm so happy to get a present.
The elevator suddenly stopped.
The taxi stopped in front of the house.
My computer keeps freezing.
I wrote a letter to my grandma.

ex.s: 생일 선물에 짧은 편지를 같이 넣었어요.
ex.en: I tucked a short letter in with the birthday present.
These days people text instead of writing letters.
It's raining, so take an umbrella.
See? I told you ahead of time.

ex.s: 그러니까 제 말은, 내일 하자는 거예요.
ex.en: I mean, what I'm saying is let's do it tomorrow.
How many hours a day do you sleep on average?
The average on this test was 70.
Rent here is higher than average.

fix.note: Usually said as 사장님, also used to address shop owners.

ex.en: Our boss is really nice.
At this restaurant, the owner does the cooking.
Excuse me, could we get some water here?

ex.s: 결혼 십 주년을 기념해서 여행 갔어요.
ex.en: We took a trip to celebrate our 10th wedding anniversary.
We ate out as a family to celebrate graduation.
Coffee is half price to celebrate the opening.

fix.en: to rise, come up; to open (eyes)

ex.en: What time does the sun come up?
The moon is out and bright tonight.
When I opened my eyes in the morning, it was ten.
I have a meeting at 10 a.m.
I'm home in the morning.
The clinic is only open Saturday mornings.
Open your book to page 50.
This page won't load.
Desserts are on the next page of the menu.

ex.s: 이 노래가 음원 순위 일 위예요.
ex.en: This song is number one on the music charts.
Our team moved up in the rankings.
I looked up restaurant rankings online.

notes: Replaced calques/unnatural lines: 도와줘서 미리 고마워요, 만나서 기뻐요 (greeting is 반가워요), 비가 멈추면 (그치다), 보통 평균 redundancy, 직업 때문에; fixed 그러니까 mistranslation.
